response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), s AS (SELECT ID, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Examination records with a NULL ID are grouped together as one group and counted in the total (NULL ID treated as its own group); the total is the count of all Examination rows.
The 'average share' is the mean of the per-ID shares (across IDs in Examination), not the share of an average ID computed some other way (these are equal: 1/number of groups).
